input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator conditional was inverted while moving the join into get_help_spec. The original was `("; " if any_prefix_is_slash else " / ")`, and the new code is `("; " if not any_prefix_is_slash else " / ")`.
- rationale: Trigger: any option with secondary opts, e.g. a boolean flag `--shout/--no-shout`. The original code joined with " / " when no slash prefix was used, but the new code joins with "; ". Help output becomes `--shout; --no-shout` instead of `--shout / --no-shout`. Options using a slash prefix such as `/debug;/no-debug` get " / " instead of "; ". The help text changes for every flag with a secondary option, and help-output tests would fail.
critique: The finding identifies the inverted condition on any_prefix_is_slash in the separator choice. It gives the same consequences as the label: '--shout; --no-shout', and ' / ' used for slash-prefixed options.
